correctness.rationale: For all integers p,q>=2, the crossing mass S is at most p. A trace-compression argument on the q-1-dimensional independent-set zero-sum subspace gives SLEM >= 1-S/q, and a normalized two-part contrast gives SLEM >= S(p+q)/(pq)-1. Their exact minimax gives S*=2pq/(q+2p) when q<=2p and S*=p otherwise. At equality of the trace bound, positive semidefiniteness forces every independent-set zero-sum vector to be a +t eigenvector, hence the cross block has constant entries along every row. For q<2p, equality in the negative two-part Rayleigh quotient forces constant cross row sums, so all cross entries are identical. For q>=2p, row saturation gives the same conclusion and zero internal edges. With uniform crossing weights, the full spectrum has two constant-on-parts modes, a q-1 dimensional +t mode, and the p-1 eigenvalues 1-qb-lambda_j(L_W), giving the necessary and sufficient clique degree and spectral bounds. Equality q=2p is treated via capacity saturation. Constructive uniform clique weights prove attainment in every regime. Exact rational tests for 70 (p,q) combinations and 1575 feasible independent-weight tests were replayed from check.py; these tests are corroborative, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The all-global-optimizer characterization, especially the necessary cross-block rigidity independent of symmetry assumptions and full internal clique Laplacian spectral interval, was not stated or implied by the located primary passages. The scalar optimum VALUE is explicitly already implied by Boyd et al. and by Jafarizadeh clique lifting from weighted star, and is not claimed novel. Existence of an optimized lifted chain does not classify all optimal matrices; the present proof exploits equality conditions to do so. Search is not proof of absolute novelty, and the residual specialized-literature risk is acknowledged.

value.rationale: A complete classification of a convex eigenvalue optimization problem on an infinite non-edge-transitive graph family gives information strictly stronger than its already-known scalar optimum: uniformity of every cross edge is forced under arbitrary asymmetry; the full nonuniform internal clique design space is described by precise degree and Laplacian eigenvalue constraints. The sharp p=q and q=2p boundaries identify when optimal internal connectivity is obligatory, optional, or impossible. This supports design with secondary requirements such as retaining an internal communication backbone without worsening mixing. It is a structural all-optimizer theorem, not an isolated trivial computation or a repackaged known objective value.
